claim: A visual change is judged by a prediction written before the edit and a blind reader after it, not by the author's own look: write hypothesis.json (observation, cause, predictions, a control that must not change), render before and after with the same poses, measure the pair, and hand only the frames to a fresh reader who has not seen the repo. Cameras must also look past and over the changed thing and from inside what is next to it.
evidence: 2026-11-17 (projects/blood-city/experiments/church-skyline/README.md): two of seven predictions failed and were the findings; the author's 'reads as a steeple' was 'plain shaft, flat top' to the blind reader near to; the owner found in a minute that lowered skies hid everything behind them, which no camera had looked at (experiments/church-roofs/README.md)
use: python -m tools.judge_experiment <dir> --pair before:after; record reviewer readings as interpretation, not measurement.
